case.title: Dinitration: approved acid-compatible microflow path
case.protocol:
RAW BATCH PROTOCOL:
An aniline derivative was treated with nitric acid in the industrial batch solvent at 60 C for 4 h. Nitric acid served as nitrating reagent and acid catalyst. The dinitrated product was obtained in 89% yield.

OBJECTIVE:
Design a conservative microflow nitration screen with segregated feeds, controlled mixing, and immediate quench.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Use only the listed inventory.
- Use two segregated feeds before the micromixer.
- Use the approved PTFE 5 mL microcoil.
- Operate at 60 C and include immediate quench.

analogies.summary: This study describes a solid acid catalyzed liquid-phase aromatic nitration reaction using concentrated nitric acid in a continuous flow system. The reaction was conducted at 120°C in dichloroethane (DCE) solvent at 1.0 M concentration using a packed-bed reactor with a volume of 7.85 mL and a flow rate of 0.91 mL/min. The flow process achieved 90% yield compared to 92% yield in the corresponding batch reaction conducted under similar conditions (120°C, 1 hour reaction time). The continuous flow approach enabled safe handling of the highly exothermic and potentially hazardous nitration reaction with concentrated nitric acid through better heat management and containment in the packed-bed reactor format. A back-pressure regulator was required to maintain proper reaction conditions and prevent solvent vaporization at the elevated temperature.

analogies.summary: This record describes a condensation reaction proceeding via nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) mechanism using DIPEA as base in DMA solvent. The reaction was performed in a Vapourtec R4+ flow reactor with a 10 mL reactor volume at 250°C with a 30-minute residence time and 1.0 mL/min flow rate, achieving 69% yield at 0.5 M concentration. The batch baseline was conducted at room temperature (25°C) for 30 minutes and achieved the same 69% yield. Flow chemistry enabled the use of significantly higher reaction temperature (250°C vs 25°C) while maintaining the same residence time and yield, suggesting improved reaction kinetics and process intensification through better heat transfer control in the continuous flow system.

chemistry.scope_summary: The synthesis involves condensation of 2-fluorobenzaldehydes with methylhydrazine to produce substituted indazoles. The reaction conditions were optimized for a range of electron-withdrawing and electron-donating groups. The methodology allows for rapid synthesis and scalability, suitable for generating a range of indazole analogues.

analogies.summary: This transition-metal-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction was performed using both homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis in acetonitrile solvent with triethylamine as base. The flow process utilized an X-Cube Flash reactor with stainless steel tubing (1.0 mm ID, 4.0 mL volume) operated at 170°C with a 10-minute residence time and 0.4 mL/min flow rate under 10 bar back pressure. Both batch (150°C, 5 hours, microwave heating) and flow conditions achieved 94% yield at 0.65 M concentration. The flow process provided a significant time advantage, reducing reaction time from 5 hours to 10 minutes (30-fold acceleration) while allowing operation at higher temperature (170°C vs 150°C) and eliminating the need for microwave heating. The back pressure regulator was essential for maintaining single-phase liquid conditions at the elevated temperature.

chemistry.scope_summary: Mizoroki–Heck couplings of aryl iodides and bromides with butyl acrylate were successfully performed in both batch/microwave and continuous-flow modes using a homogeneous Pd(OAc)2 catalyst with high yield and selectivity.

optimization_table.key_findings: The Mizoroki–Heck coupling using 0.01 mol % Pd(OAc)2 at 170°C achieved full conversion and high selectivity.

proposal.chemistry_notes: Thermal nitration of aniline derivative. Highly exothermic; flow mitigates thermal runaway. PTFE wetted path required for nitric acid compatibility. No light source used. Quench is critical for safety and selectivity. Residence time reduced from 4h batch to ~19 min based on kinetic intensification factor.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Calculation Step 2 estimated 18.8 min (range 10.3-36.0 min) based on 13x intensification factor. Analogy 1 used 60 min at 120C; our T is lower (60C) but flow mixing is superior. 18.8 min is conservative and within calculated range.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Single-phase liquid system. Basis is liquid volume / liquid flow.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: From Batch Protocol and Chemistry Plan: 60 C. Analogy 1 used 120C but different solvent/catalyst. We maintain batch T for selectivity control.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Calculation Step 8: BPR not required. T=60C is well below solvent bp (assumed >80C for industrial solvent) and no gas generated. Inventory BPR available but not strictly needed for pressure containment, though could be used for stability. Set to 0 as per calculation.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: From Inventory: PTFE. Chemistry Plan notes PTFE is compatible with nitric acid. Analogy 1 used packed bed (material unspecified but likely ceramic/glass); PTFE is safer for HNO3.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: From Batch Protocol: 0.1 M. Analogy 1 used 1.0 M; we stick to batch concentration to ensure solubility and control exotherm density.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: From Inventory: 5 mL PTFE microcoil. Calculation Step 3 suggested 9.41 mL for 1.0 mm ID, but Inventory mandates 5 mL reactor. With 5 mL and 0.5 mL/min flow, tau = 10 min. This is within the lower bound of the calculated range (10.3-36.0 min) and provides higher throughput. Note: 10 min is slightly below the 18.8 min target, but acceptable for a screen.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Derived from Inventory Reactor Volume (5 mL) and Target Residence Time. To achieve ~10-19 min tau with 5 mL reactor, flow must be 0.26-0.5 mL/min. Set to 0.5 mL/min (max practical for syringe pumps in inventory) to maximize throughput while keeping tau ~10 min. This is a conservative screen condition.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: From Inventory: 0.5 mm. Calculation Step 3 suggested 1.0 mm, but Inventory mandates 0.5 mm. This increases pressure drop but improves heat transfer.
